config.title: CSS custom properties (variables)

intro.title: CSS custom properties (variables)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a themed color scheme that you can change dynamically using CSS custom properties (also called CSS variables). You will learn how to define reusable values with custom properties and apply them to style elements like backgrounds and text. The core concept involves declaring variables in a CSS rule, referencing them with the var() function, and updating them for real-time style changes. You will work with basic CSS selectors, properties, and the :root pseudo-class to create a maintainable and flexible design. By the end, you will understand how CSS variables help streamline styling and enable easy theme adjustments.
intro.usecase: CSS custom properties are essential for creating maintainable design systems in real-world applications. They're used extensively in component libraries like Material-UI or Bootstrap to define consistent color schemes, spacing, and typography across entire applications. For example, a dashboard might use custom properties to manage theme switching between light and dark modes, where changing a single variable like --primary-color updates all buttons, cards, and text throughout the interface. Developers also use them in responsive designs to adjust layout properties like --grid-gap or --sidebar-width based on screen size, ensuring consistent behavior across different components without duplicating code.

objectives: Declare CSS custom properties in a root selector
Apply custom properties to style elements
Update custom property values using JavaScript
Construct responsive designs with custom property fallbacks
Manipulate custom properties for dynamic theming
Integrate custom properties with CSS calc() function

steps.title: Define a CSS custom property (variable) on the :root pseudo-class
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for the :root pseudo-class and declare a custom property named --primary-color with the value #3498db.
steps.hint: The :root selector targets the highest-level element in the document (like html). Inside its rule, use the syntax --property-name: value; to define a custom property.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your CSS rule for :root here */
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a CSS custom property named --primary-color with the value #3498db, declared globally using the :root selector.
successCriteria: The :root selector is used, and inside it, a custom property --primary-color is declared with the value #3498db.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the :root selector and the correct syntax --primary-color: #3498db; inside the rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to create a rule for :root and declare the custom property with the exact name and value.

steps.title: Use the var() function to apply the custom property to an element
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for the .box class that sets the background-color property using var(--primary-color).
steps.hint: Use the var() function to reference the custom property you defined on :root. The syntax is: property: var(--custom-property-name);
steps.seedCode:
/* Add your CSS rule for :root here */

/* Create a CSS rule for .box here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have its background-color set to the value of --primary-color using the var() function.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .box exists and sets background-color using var(--primary-color).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the var() function correctly with the custom property name.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a CSS rule for .box that sets background-color using var(--primary-color).

steps.title: Create a second custom property for text color
steps.instruction: In the existing :root rule, add a second custom property named --text-color with the value #ffffff.
steps.hint: Add the property declaration after the existing one, separated by a semicolon.
steps.expectedOutcome: The :root rule will contain two custom properties: --main-color and --text-color.
successCriteria: The :root rule includes a custom property named --text-color with value #ffffff.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a custom property, but check the name or value. It should be --text-color: #ffffff;
steps.feedbackWrong: The :root rule should contain --text-color: #ffffff;. Try adding it after the existing property.

steps.title: Apply multiple custom properties to style text
steps.instruction: In the .box class rule, add the CSS property color with the value var(--text-color) and the property padding with the value 20px.
steps.hint: You can add multiple CSS properties to the same selector by separating them with semicolons. Use the var() function to apply your custom property for text color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have a blue background, dark text color, and 20px of padding around its content.
successCriteria: The .box selector includes both color: var(--text-color) and padding: 20px properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the color property using var(--text-color) and the padding property with 20px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box rule should include both color: var(--text-color) and padding: 20px properties. Check your syntax and property names.

steps.title: Define a custom property with a fallback value
steps.instruction: Add a third custom property named --border-radius with the value 8px to the existing :root rule.
steps.hint: Inside the :root rule, add a new line with --border-radius: 8px;
steps.expectedOutcome: The :root rule will have three custom properties defined, including the new --border-radius property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a custom property, but check the name and value. It should be --border-radius: 8px;
steps.feedbackWrong: The :root rule should include --border-radius: 8px;. Try adding it on a new line inside the :root rule.

steps.title: Use var() with a fallback value parameter
steps.instruction: In the .box class rule, add the property border-radius: var(--border-radius, 4px);
steps.hint: The var() function can accept a second parameter as a fallback value. If the custom property --border-radius is not defined, the browser will use 4px instead.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box rule will now include a border-radius property that uses the custom property --border-radius if defined, otherwise falls back to 4px.
successCriteria: The .box class rule contains the property border-radius: var(--border-radius, 4px);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the border-radius property exactly as specified: border-radius: var(--border-radius, 4px);
steps.feedbackWrong: The border-radius property with var() and a fallback value wasn't added correctly. Check that you've written border-radius: var(--border-radius, 4px); inside the .box rule.

steps.title: Override a custom property at element level
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for .special-box that redefines --main-color with the value #e74c3c
steps.hint: Add a new CSS selector .special-box and set --main-color inside it to override the global value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .special-box selector will have a custom property --main-color set to #e74c3c, overriding the global value for elements with that class.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .special-box exists and sets --main-color: #e74c3c;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .special-box rule, but make sure it sets --main-color: #e74c3c; exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a CSS rule for .special-box that redefines --main-color with the value #e74c3c. Check your syntax and property name.

steps.title: Apply the overridden custom property to a specific element
steps.instruction: Add the .special-box class selector and set its background-color property to use the --primary-color custom property with var()
steps.hint: Create a new CSS rule that targets the .special-box class and uses var(--primary-color) as the background-color value
steps.expectedOutcome: The .special-box selector will be created and will use the --primary-color custom property for its background color
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .special-box selector with background-color: var(--primary-color)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using var(--primary-color) as the value for background-color in the .special-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .special-box rule should be created with background-color: var(--primary-color). Check that you've written the selector and property correctly.

steps.title: Use custom properties in calc() expressions
steps.instruction: Add a fourth custom property named --spacing with the value 10px to the :root selector.
steps.hint: Remember to define the custom property inside the :root rule, using the same syntax as previous properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The :root selector will contain a new --spacing custom property set to 10px.
successCriteria: A custom property named --spacing with value 10px is added to the :root rule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added --spacing: 10px; inside the :root rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The custom property --spacing with value 10px was not found in the :root selector. Try again.

steps.title: Create responsive custom properties using media queries
steps.instruction: Add a media query for max-width: 768px that redefines --spacing with value 5px on the :root
steps.hint: Use @media (max-width: 768px) { :root { --spacing: 5px; } } after your existing CSS rules.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will contain a media query that changes the --spacing custom property value to 5px when the viewport is 768px or narrower.
successCriteria: A media query with (max-width: 768px) is added, and inside it, :root redefines --spacing: 5px;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your media query targets max-width: 768px and redefines --spacing: 5px on the :root selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query wasn't added correctly. Remember to use @media (max-width: 768px) { :root { --spacing: 5px; } }
